payload.attack: The hypothesis characterizes standard GAAP-compliant revenue recognition as aggressive manipulation without any supporting evidence of valuation impropriety, restatements, or regulatory action. Under ASC 606, Netcapital is required to recognize non-cash consideration at fair value upon receipt, and under ASC 321/820, it must adjust these holdings to fair value each period. Furthermore, the elevated Beneish M-Scores are driven by Sales Growth Index (SGI) and Days Sales in Receivables Index (DSRI), which are natural consequences of Netcapital's rapid expansion and business model, and represent a recognized high false-positive rate rather than proof of manipulation.

While GAAP compliance dictates the accounting entries, labeling the extreme divergence between net income and cash flow as entirely innocent is premature. The massive non-cash gaps (reaching 100% and 119% of total revenue in FY21 and FY22) depend entirely on highly subjective Level 3 fair value estimates of illiquid startup equity. The realized loss of $406,060 on an investment sale (E13) demonstrates that these holdings are prone to significant value erosion upon liquidation, and the absence of complete filings (E11, E14) prevents a full evaluation of long-term asset impairments.
